AgentToolsPolicy.description: Whether members' coding clients may run their agent tools.
AgentToolsPolicy.title: AgentToolsPolicy

AnnouncementChanges.description:
Only the fields sent change. `end_now` sets `ends_at` to the server's
clock rather than the operator's, which is what "end now" means.
AnnouncementChanges.title: AnnouncementChanges

ApplyBody.description:
One move on the ladder. The reason is for the person it concerns;
the notes are the operator's own. Evidence is report and flag ids.
ApplyBody.title: ApplyBody

AssistantMessage.description: `content` is null on a pure tool-call turn, as OpenAI shapes it.
AssistantMessage.title: AssistantMessage

Unknown fields are ignored, as OpenAI does (the versioning rule in

ChatCompletionRequest.title: ChatCompletionRequest

CompactConversation.title: CompactConversation

One element of the array-of-parts content form. `text` and

model takes images (`message_content`), and the rest are refused by
name.

Each count is null when the server does not know it: the window when
the model states none, the counts when the upstream reported no usage.
ContextEvent.title: ContextEvent

One thread's system prompt. `null` or "" clears it, falling the
conversation back to the user's instructions and then the org's.
ConversationInstructionsBody.title: ConversationInstructionsBody

A message as the conversation routes return it (`store.Message.to_dict`):

Without `credentials` the connection is made `pending`: its ingress

with the credentials activates it.

Text for the open part at `index`: `content` for a text part,
`reasoning` for a reasoning part; one of the two.
DeltaEvent.title: DeltaEvent

EditMessage.title: EditMessage

OpenAI's `POST /v1/embeddings` body. `model` is accepted for client
compatibility (every SDK sends one) but the deployment's configured
embedding model is what goes upstream: there is exactly one, and a
caller naming another gets a 404 saying so rather than a gateway error.
EmbeddingsRequest.title: EmbeddingsRequest

ErrorEvent.description:
The turn failed after the 200. `code` is `budget` when the
organisation cannot buy the turn; absent for an upstream failure or a
resume that found nothing to resume.
ErrorEvent.title: ErrorEvent

ImageUrl.description:
OpenAI's `image_url` object: a `data:` URI or an `https://` URL, and
the optional `detail` hint, relayed to the gateway as given.

OpenAI's `response_format.json_schema`. The schema itself is relayed
untouched -- whether it is a schema the gateway can enforce is the
gateway's verdict, surfaced as a 400 with its reason -- but it has to be
an object, and it has to have the name OpenAI requires.
JsonSchemaSpec.title: JsonSchemaSpec

MatterWave's extras ride under `metadata`, which OpenAI reserves for
caller-defined key/values, so the request stays valid for any client.
`conversation_id` opts a call into persistence (stateless
by default).
Metadata.title: Metadata

ModelPolicy.description:
`allowed` is the ids the org's members may use, or null for every
model the plan permits. The house model is added back whatever is sent
(org_settings.org_permits says why), so it never has to be listed.
ModelPolicy.title: ModelPolicy

MoveBody.description:
`null` is the main list. The field is required so an empty body
cannot be mistaken for "unfile".
MoveBody.title: MoveBody

OrgInstructionsBody.description: The org level: one block of text an admin sets for everyone.
OrgInstructionsBody.title: OrgInstructionsBody

PartStartEvent.description:
A part of the assistant message opens at `index`. A `tool_call` part
carries `id`, `name` and `arguments`; a `tool_result` its call's `id`,
`output` and `is_error`; `text` and `reasoning` only the index.
PartStartEvent.title: PartStartEvent

PasswordChange.description:
Bounds only: the length floor is a 400 with a code, not a 422, so
the form treats it like the provider's policy refusal.
PasswordChange.title: PasswordChange

Proof.description:
A code OR a recovery code. Neither is a 422 before anything is
checked; both is the code (the recovery code is kept for when the
authenticator is gone, and a request carrying both has one).
Proof.title: Proof

PutDunningPolicy.description:
An org's own late-payment policy. Every field is optional and an
absent one inherits the platform default; all absent clears the
override. The ceilings are checked by dunning.check_override, which
knows them.
PutDunningPolicy.title: PutDunningPolicy

PutStripePrices.description:
The two price ids for one plan. Either may be cleared with null --
that is how a plan is withdrawn from sale without deleting its row.
PutStripePrices.title: PutStripePrices

RegenerateMessage.description: Regenerate takes no content -- the prompt is the branch above it.
RegenerateMessage.title: RegenerateMessage

ReportBody.description:
What a user sends when they press Report.

Two kinds, not a taxonomy: `unsafe` routes to review and
`unhelpful` routes to the product backlog. Most reports are the second
kind -- including refusal complaints -- and merging them
buries the rare serious one.
ReportBody.title: ReportBody

RequestToolCall.description:
A tool call the assistant made earlier in the conversation, echoed
back by the caller with its `tool` result -- the second half of the
round trip. Relayed to the gateway in the same shape.
RequestToolCall.title: RequestToolCall

ResolveBody.description:
A reviewer's conclusion, in their own words. Required: a report
closed with no reason recorded is a report nobody can audit later.
ResolveBody.title: ResolveBody

ReviewBody.description:
A reviewer's decision on one report. The note is required for every
action, including dismissal: a report closed with nothing written is a
report nobody can audit later. For warn/limit/suspend the note is also
the reason shown to the account.
ReviewBody.title: ReviewBody

Rollout.description: Targeting for a flag that is not on for everyone.
Rollout.title: Rollout

RotateSecret.description:
How long the old secret keeps signing beside the new one. Zero ends
it now: the choice for a secret that leaked.
RotateSecret.title: RotateSecret

ShareCreate.description:
How long the link lives, in seconds, or null for until revoked. The
SPA offers presets; the API takes the number so a client can pick any
span inside the bounds. `include_attachments` is off unless asked: a
reader then sees each attachment's name and nothing else.
ShareCreate.title: ShareCreate

ToolCallFragment.description:
One streamed piece of a tool call: the first for an `index` carries
`id`, `type` and the name, the rest carry `arguments` to concatenate.
ToolCallFragment.title: ToolCallFragment

ToolSpec.description:
One `tools[]` entry. Function tools only, which is all OpenAI's chat
completions define; the shape is relayed to the gateway as given.
ToolSpec.title: ToolSpec

UpdateConnection.description:
Every field optional: omitted means unchanged. An admin may switch a
connection on or off; `revoked` and `error` are the provider's to set,
and switching one back on is `active`.
UpdateConnection.title: UpdateConnection

UpdateConversation.description:
What PATCH may change: the title, the default model, the preset.

`default_model` is the picker's selection, persisted as the
conversation's default. `null` clears it back to the configured default;
omitting the field entirely is "nothing to update" -- `model_fields_set`
tells the two apart, which a plain default of None cannot.

`title` is the person's name for the conversation, 1-200 characters once
the surrounding whitespace is gone. There is no "clear" for it: a
conversation always has a title, so `null` here is the same as leaving
the field out.

`preset_id` puts the conversation on one of the org's live presets, and
`null` takes it off again, back to its own model and instructions --
told apart from an omitted field the way `default_model` is.
UpdateConversation.title: UpdateConversation

UpdateEndpoint.description: Every field optional: omitted means unchanged.
UpdateEndpoint.title: UpdateEndpoint

UpdateIdentity.description: `map` names the member in `subject`; the others take none.
UpdateIdentity.title: UpdateIdentity

UpdateKey.description:
A PATCH body: a field left out is left alone, a field sent as null
is cleared (no expiry, any network, the platform's limit, the default
scopes). `model_fields_set` is how the route tells the two apart.
UpdateKey.title: UpdateKey

UpdatePreset.title: UpdatePreset

UserInstructionsBody.description:
The two fields people expect. Capped here, on the way
in, so a user is told their text is too long instead of silently losing
the tail of it at assembly. See instructions.py for the numbers.
UserInstructionsBody.title: UserInstructionsBody

matterwave__routes_admin__PutPlan.description:
The editable half of a plans row. `limits` is validated against
FREE_LIMITS' shape in plans.validate_limits, not here: the shape is the
catalog's to define, and pydantic would have to copy it.
matterwave__routes_admin__PutPlan.title: PutPlan

apiKey.description: A MatterWave API key (`mw_...`), created under Settings > API keys or by device login. A key carries scopes; an operation that needs one lists it, and an empty list means any key. `/api/conversations*` needs `chat:read` for a GET and `chat:write` otherwise; `/api/org/webhooks*` needs `webhooks:manage`, `/api/org/usage*` `usage:read`, and `/api/org/presets*` `chat:read` for a GET and `presets:manage` otherwise, on top of the owner's org role. Known scopes: `chat:read`, `chat:write`, `keys:manage`, `presets:manage`, `usage:read`, `webhooks:manage`.

idpToken.description: An access token from the deployment's identity provider, for an agent or a service account. Treated as the person it names, like a session.

sessionCookie.description: The browser session set at sign-in. Non-GET requests also need the `mw_csrf` cookie's value in the `X-CSRF-Token` header.
sessionCookie.name: mw_session

info.description: Everything a signed-in person or a script can do: the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` surface plus the native `/api` routes the web app is built on, filed by area. Each operation lists the credentials it accepts. A script presents a MatterWave API key as a bearer token; routes that manage the organisation (members, SSO, billing, the audit log) refuse a key and need a person's session or IdP token. Webhooks and the org usage report take a key with `webhooks:manage` or `usage:read` whose owner holds the org role the route asks of a session. A cookie session must echo the `mw_csrf` cookie in `X-CSRF-Token` on every non-GET request. Every response carries `X-Request-Id`. `/v1` is the stable contract; the native routes follow the same additive-only rule but are not versioned by path.
info.title: MatterWave native API

x-stability.promise: Additive changes only within v1: no field is removed or retyped, deprecations carry Deprecation and Sunset headers with 12 months notice, and clients must tolerate unknown fields.

get.description:
Who is signed in on this browser, acting one first. Anonymous on
purpose: after signing out of the acting account the front door
offers the parked ones, and there is no principal to ask as. Answers
only what the envelopes already told this browser -- an email, a
name, an org name -- never account data.

schema.title: Response List Accounts Api Accounts Get

post.description:
Every account on this browser, acting and parked: each row revoked,
each cookie cleared. The answer carries the provider's end_session
endpoint as /api/logout does, so the SPA finishes the same way.

schema.title: Response Logout All Api Accounts Logout All Post

post.description:
Make a parked account the acting one. Both envelopes are verified
before either cookie is written: the one coming in must be signed,
unexpired and unrevoked, or it is dropped instead and the caller
told; the one going out is parked only if it is still good, else
the slot is simply freed. The SPA reloads afterwards, so no state of
the previous account survives in the page.

schema.title: Response Switch Account Api Accounts Switch Post

post.description:
Sign one PARKED account out: revoke its row, drop its cookie, leave
every other account as it is. The acting account signs out through
/api/logout, as before.

schema.title: Response Logout Parked Api Accounts  Slot  Logout Post

get.description: The announcements inside their window, most severe first.

schema.title: Response Active Announcements Api Announcements Get

post.description:
Accept one file and return its attachment row.

The response carries a freshly-minted download URL so the composer can
render a thumbnail without a second round trip -- and because the URL is
minted here rather than stored, that is the only place it can come from.

`file.content_type` is received and **never read**. Starlette parses it
from the multipart part header, which is the client's string; the type is
decided from the bytes in `sniff.sniff`.

schema.title: Response Upload Attachment Api Attachments Post

get.description:
What this user may still upload, so the composer can say so up front
rather than after a 413.

schema.title: Response My Limits Api Attachments Limits Me Get

delete.description:
Mark one attachment deleted. The blob goes on the sweeper's next pass.

The response says so rather than claiming the bytes are gone: the
deletion promise has to be honest, and "deleted" when the
object still exists for up to an hour is the kind of half-truth that makes
a privacy policy wrong.

schema.title: Response Delete Attachment Api Attachments  Attachment Id  Delete

get.description: One attachment's metadata, with a fresh download URL.

schema.title: Response Get Attachment Api Attachments  Attachment Id  Get

get.description:
The bytes, behind a valid signature AND the caller's own session.

**Both**, not either. The signature alone would make the URL a bearer
token that works from any browser; the session alone would make the
signature decorative. Requiring both means a leaked URL is useless without
the session, and a session is useless without a URL minted for it.

`store.get` re-checks the org and subject in SQL, and `open_blob`
re-checks `scan_status = 'clean'` before any bytes are opened. Three
independent gates for one read, which is what "unreachable by
construction" costs.

`{"scan_status": ...}` for one of the caller's own uploads.

The composer polls this while a chip says "scanning". Scoped to org AND
subject in SQL like every other attachment read, and a 404 for any row
that is not the caller's -- the same one answer `GET /{id}` gives, so this
route is not an oracle for ids in other tenants either.

schema.title: Response Attachment Scan Status Api Attachments  Attachment Id  Scan Get

get.description: Redirect to a freshly-minted signed URL for this attachment. What an `` in the transcript points at. The SPA cannot sign (the secret is server-side) and should not have to fetch metadata first just to render a thumbnail, so this route does the mint and redirects -- which is the same two round trips the browser would have made anyway, without the SPA having to orchestrate them. The redirect is **302, never cached**: the URL it points at expires in ten minutes, and a cached 301 would pin a stale one into the browser forever. The signature still carries the caller's subject, so following the redirect without the session is a 403 exactly as it is on the direct path.

post.description:
Mint the device's key for the person approving and park it for one
poll. A device key, on any plan: this is how a person signs a terminal
or an editor in, not a key they minted, so the `api_keys` feature that
gates `POST /api/keys` is not asked. The late-payment pause on new
keys is, as it is of the Settings form.

A device that never polls again leaves an unused key behind, listed
and revocable like any other; its plaintext is gone with the code.

schema.title: Response Approve Device Login Api Auth Device Approve Post
Response Deny Device Login Api Auth Device Deny Post

post.description:
Which client is asking, for the approval page to show. Counted with
the decisions: a lookup is how a guess would be tested.

schema.title: Response Lookup Device Login Api Auth Device Lookup Post

post.description:
The browser's assertion, to the provider's session the challenge
names; then the same finalize the password route does, and the same
redirect into /api/auth/callback. The suspension and verification
gates run after the proof, as on the password path: a refused
assertion must not become an oracle for the account's state.

The request options for `navigator.credentials.get`, with the
provider's session for this sign-in sealed beside them.

By address, because the provider opens the session for a named user
and lists that user's credentials in the options. An address with no
account and an account with no passkey get the same 404, so the
answer says nothing about which addresses exist. The browser's
conditional UI (a passkey offered in the address field's autofill)
is not offered: it needs options minted before the address is known,
which this relay cannot ask the provider for.

Begin a subscription. Returns the Stripe Checkout URL to redirect to.

**Owner or admin only, and authenticated.** A session is required to
reach this: an unauthenticated endpoint that mints Checkout Sessions is
a card-testing target, and the org is taken from the membership rather
than the body so a caller cannot start a subscription for someone else.

get.description:
The org's invoices, newest first: status, amount, due date and
Stripe's PDF and hosted-page links. Owner or admin, like the portal:
the hosted page is where an invoice is paid.

schema.title: Response Billing Invoices Api Billing Invoices Get

A Stripe customer portal session: card update, plan change, cancel.

The portal rather than a page of our own: self-service
cancellation is the single biggest dispute preventer, and what it
allows is Dashboard configuration instead of code we would own.

schema.title: Response Open Portal Api Billing Portal Post

get.description:
What the UI needs to render a billing page, in one call.

Deliberately readable by any member, not just an admin: a non-admin
should see the org's plan and be told to ask an admin, rather than get
a 403 that looks like a bug. The admin-only facts (the portal URL, the
event trail) are on their own endpoints.

schema.title: Response Billing Status Api Billing Status Get

get.description:
The org's allowance, usage, overage and cap, so the UI can warn
before a hard stop. Any member may read it: a user must be able to see
the balance that will stop their request -- including their own cap
(`member_cap`, null when none applies) and what they have spent against
it this period (`member_spent`), both in micro-dollars at list price.

schema.title: Response Get Budget Api Budget Get

put.description:
Set the overage cap. Owner or admin only: the cap is the org's
exposure past what the plan includes.

With virtual keys on, the org's LiteLLM key and team follow the new
cap, so the upstream backstop matches what the UI shows. The local row
is written first: the app's own gate is the one a user hits, and a
failed upstream resize is a 502 the admin sees, not a silent split.

schema.title: Response Put Budget Api Budget Put

The per-member caps and spend. Owner or admin only: what a colleague
spent is the org's business, the same line /api/org/usage draws.

schema.title: Response Get Member Budgets Api Budget Members Get

Set the default cap every member without their own is held to.
Owner or admin only. Audited like the overage cap: it decides whose
requests are refused.

schema.title: Response Put Member Default Cap Api Budget Members Put

Set or remove one member's own cap. Owner or admin only, and only
for a current member: a cap on a subject nobody holds would be a row
nothing reads.

schema.title: Response Put Member Cap Api Budget Members  Subject  Put

get.description:
The sidebar list, one page at a time. `filter` selects the archive
slice, `cursor` resumes where the previous page's `next_cursor` left off
and `next_cursor` is null on the last page; scoping and soft delete are
the store's, on every branch. One row past the page is read so "is there
more" is answered without a count.

schema.title: Response List Conversations Api Conversations Get
Response Create Conversation Api Conversations Post

Full-text search over the caller's own messages.

Declared above `/{conversation_id}`: FastAPI matches in declaration order,
and a dynamic segment registered first would swallow the literal "search"
and answer 404 for every query.

Org- and owner-scoping and `deleted_at IS NULL` are the store's, like
every other read -- no SQL and no tenancy predicate lives in this file
(AGENTS.md). An empty `q` is an empty result, not a 422: the SPA clears
the box by sending one, and an error toast for "the user deleted their
query" is noise.

Response Delete Conversation Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Delete

The conversation and its messages.

`messages` is the active path -- one path through the tree,
which is what the transcript renders. `?full=1` adds `tree`, every message
including the siblings the path leaves out, for a client that wants the
switcher without a second request.

schema.title: Response Get Conversation Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Get

patch.description:
Rename the conversation, set or clear its default model, put it on a
preset or take it off one -- any of them at once.

The tenancy check is the store's, same as every other conversation write;
a row the caller cannot see is a 404 for a rename exactly as for a
delete. Permission over WHICH models may be picked is not done here --
that is org policy, and per-org model policy does not exist yet.

A rename is the person's choice, and the store records it as one so the
auto-title never overwrites it. No webhook event: a title is the person's
text, and `conversation.created` deliberately carries none of it either.

schema.title: Response Update Conversation Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Patch

Switch the thread to another branch.

A cursor move, not a write to the tree: the same messages exist before and
after, and only which path `list_messages` returns changes. The store
refuses a leaf from another conversation, so the 404 covers both "no such
conversation" and "not a message of it" -- indistinguishable to the
caller, as everywhere else.

Response Unarchive Conversation Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Archive Delete

Archive is not delete: the row keeps `deleted_at`
NULL, stays readable, and stays searchable. It only leaves the default
list.

post.description:
Fold the older turns of the active path now, without a user turn.

The same fold a send runs when the next turn would not fit, under the
same plan gate and budget. Returns the summary message, which is the new
leaf. 409 when there is nothing to fold -- the path holds no more than
the kept pairs after its latest summary -- when the model has no known
window to size the summary against, or when compaction is switched off; 402 when the org cannot buy it; 502
when the model could not summarise, in which case nothing was written.

schema.title: Response Compact Conversation Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Compact Post

get.description:
How full the active path is, for a client that draws a meter without
a stream (a terminal, an editor panel).

`used_tokens` is the last real count on the path after its latest
summary; with none yet, the summary's own `tokens_after` estimate, and
`estimated` says which. Null when nothing is known. `context_window` is
null when the model states none, and then there is no meter to draw.
`keep_pairs` is how many recent user/assistant pairs a fold of this path
would keep: the most recent that fit MW_COMPACTION_KEEP_SHARE of the
window, at most MW_COMPACTION_KEEP_PAIRS, at least one.

schema.title: Response Conversation Context Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Context Get

get.description:
The caller's own ratings in this conversation, so the thumbs show
their state on reload. Nobody else's: the aggregate is not a reader's
business, and the operator view of it is a separate feature.

schema.title: Response List Feedback Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Feedback Get

post.description:
Copy the path down to a message into a new conversation.

A snapshot with new ids in the caller's own org, so a branch can become
its own thread and later edits to either side leave the other alone.

schema.title: Response Fork Conversation Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Fork Post

put.description:
Set or clear this thread's own prompt, overriding the user's for it.

The owner check is the conversation store's tenancy filter, exactly as for
the title and the default model: a caller who cannot see the row cannot
write it, and gets the same 404 rather than a 403 that would confirm the
row exists.

schema.title: Response Put Conversation Instructions Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Instructions Put

post.description:
Append a user message and stream the assistant's reply as SSE.

POST rather than GET because it creates state, which means the browser uses
`fetch()` + ReadableStream rather than `EventSource`. That is fine, and it
keeps the request body available for the prompt. `fetch()` also loses
EventSource's automatic reconnect -- deliberately, because silently
re-sending a prompt would bill twice; a client that wants the rest of a
turn re-presents `Last-Event-ID` instead.

The turn itself is `open_turn`'s, shared with the connector job.

Edit a user message: a sibling with the new text, and a fresh answer
under it. The original message and everything under it stay
exactly where they were -- that is what makes the switcher meaningful.

Streams the new assistant turn exactly as `send_message` does, through the
same `run_generation`.

Answer again: a sibling of this assistant message under the same user
turn. An overwrite would lose the answer the reader may
still prefer, so this is an insert like every other branch.

schema.title: Response Unpin Conversation Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Pin Delete

put.description: 409 for a temporary conversation: pinning is keeping.

schema.title: Response Pin Conversation Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Pin Put

post.description:
Report a conversation or a message in it.

**This is a legal artefact, not a UX affordance.** It is the mechanism by
which "actual knowledge" is obtained for 18 U.S.C. 2258A purposes, which
is why the handler's only job is to make the report durable and why it
refuses outright (503) rather than accepting when there is no database to
store it in. A button that returns 201 and drops the report is worse than
no button: it tells a user who saw something serious that it has been
dealt with.

What it deliberately does NOT do:

* **It does not place a legal hold.** A hold is a human decision with a
  documented reason and a review date, and a self-service
  endpoint that pinned content forever would let any user make any
  conversation unpurgeable -- and would make the retention promise false
  for anyone who got reported.
* **It does not suspend or action the reported account.** Rungs above
  throttle are human decisions, and a report is an allegation.
* **It does not notify NCMEC.** That path requires registration that does
  not exist (moderation.py, MODERATION_NOT_CONFIGURED item 2), and a
  function pretending to file a CyberTipline report would be the single
  most dangerous stub in this codebase.

The review step is a person reading `open_reports`, on the clock the
escalation runbook states (docs/runbooks/moderation-escalation.md).

schema.title: Response Report Conversation Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Report Post

post.description:
Snapshot the active path and mint a link to it.

The token is in this response and nowhere else: the store keeps its
hash, the list below never includes it, and a person who loses the
link makes another. `path` is the SPA route the link opens; the SPA
prefixes its own origin, which it knows and the API only infers.
Refused when the org has switched sharing off, and rate-limited per
person, because a public origin that mints links is a hosting service
for whoever can script it.

schema.title: Response Create Share Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Share Post
Response List Conversation Shares Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Shares Get

get.description:
Every message in the conversation, for the branch switcher.

The transcript reads one path; the switcher needs the siblings that path
deliberately leaves out. Creation order, so a client can rebuild the tree
from `parent_id` without sorting.

schema.title: Response Get Conversation Tree Api Conversations  Conversation Id  Tree Get

get.description:

turn off per plan. Gated on creation only -- listing and revoking stay

always have. A revoked key is a 404 like a missing one -- revocation is

owner or an org owner/admin may edit it (`_require_may_change`).

reports as `previous_valid_until`, so a deploy can swap the value.

still be able to replace a key it believes leaked. A revoked key cannot
be rotated (404, like a missing one) -- revocation is final, and a
rotation that revived it would make it not so.

What this API is and what it promises: the release, the endpoints,
what this deployment can do (`capabilities`) and the stability rule for
`/v1`. Needs no key, so a client can decide whether it can talk to this
deployment before it holds one.

200.description: What `/v1` is and what it promises.

post.description:
Send a conversation and get the model's reply, as one `chat.completion`
object or, with `stream: true`, a stream of `chat.completion.chunk`
events. OpenAI's request and response shapes; `model` may be omitted for
the deployment's default.

The request's `messages` are the whole prompt. With
`metadata.conversation_id` the turn is also recorded into that
conversation, tool rounds included: the assistant's `tool_calls` and
the `tool` messages that answer them are stored as `tool_call` and
`tool_result` parts of one assistant message, as the server's own tool
turns are, and history a request repeats is not stored again. Stored
history is never added to the prompt: the caller owns the context, as
every OpenAI client assumes.

`tools`, `tool_choice` and `response_format` go to the model as sent and
what comes back is relayed: tool calls arrive in `message.tool_calls` (or
streamed `delta.tool_calls`) for the caller to run, never run here. A
`tool_choice` that demanded a call the model did not make is a 400
`tool_calls_unsupported`, not prose parsed as an answer.

requestBody.description: OpenAI's chat-completion request. Unknown fields are ignored; `functions`, `function_call` and `n` other than 1 are refused with 400 `unsupported_parameter` rather than ignored. `tools`, `tool_choice` and `response_format` go to the model as sent and what comes back is relayed: tool calls are returned for the caller to run, never run here. `metadata.conversation_id` records the turn into that conversation; the request's `messages` are still the whole prompt.

200.description: The completion. With `stream: false` one `chat.completion` object; with `stream: true` a `text/event-stream` of `data:` lines, each a `chat.completion.chunk`, ending in `data: [DONE]`. A failure after the stream has started is sent as an error envelope on its own `data:` line. With `stream_options.include_usage` the last chunk before `[DONE]` carries `usage` and an empty `choices`.

400.description: A malformed body (`invalid_value`), an unsupported parameter (`unsupported_parameter`), an image part (`unsupported_content_part`), a `tool_choice` that demanded a call the model did not make (`tool_calls_unsupported`), or a request the model gateway itself rejected, with its reason (`upstream_rejected`).

401.description: No key, or an invalid, expired or revoked one (`authentication_error` / `invalid_api_key`).

403.description: The key lacks the `chat:write` scope (`permission_error` / `insufficient_scope`), or the account is suspended (`account_suspended`).

404.description: A model the gateway does not serve (`model_not_found`), or a `metadata.conversation_id` that is not the key owner's (`conversation_not_found`).

429.description: More than 60 requests a minute on one key (`rate_limit_error` / `rate_limit_exceeded`, with `Retry-After`), or the organisation's monthly budget is used up (`insufficient_quota`).

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the next request.

/api/conversations/{conversation_id}/mes.description: Named events (`event:` plus one `data:` line of JSON), ending after `done`, `error` or `moderation_block`. `: mw-heartbeat` comments arrive between frames. The frames of the generation itself carry `id: <generation>:<seq>`; a client whose body drops re-sends the request with `Last-Event-ID` set to the last one seen and the server replays the rest of the same generation rather than starting another.

compacting.description: First, on a send that folds earlier turns before it: the summary is decoded before the answer can start, so a client restarts its wait for the first token here. `compaction` or `notice` follows.

compaction.description: Earlier turns were folded into `message`, a `system` message with one `summary` part, before this turn was sent. Sent ahead of `message` when the next prompt would not fit the model's window.

context.description: The turn's real token counts, for a context meter; just before `done`, whenever the window or the counts are known. Carries `id:`.

delta.description: Text for the open part. Carries `id:`.

done.description: The turn ended; the saved assistant message, `truncated: true` and `finish_reason: length` when the model's token limit cut it.

error.description: The turn failed after the 200: the upstream died (what arrived is saved as a truncated message), the budget is spent, or a `Last-Event-ID` resolved to nothing.

message.description: The user message this turn appended (or the edited one), as saved.

moderation_block.description: MatterWave would not send this message to a model -- a different fact from the model declining to answer, so a different frame. Nothing was appended. `request_id` is the one to quote.

notice.description: Something the person should be told that is not part of the answer: a fold that could not run (`code: compaction`), after which the turn runs uncompacted, or a branch over the limit that an edit or regenerate cannot fold.

part_start.description: A part of the assistant message opens. Carries `id:`.

title.description: The conversation was named from this turn's first line.

/api/conversations/{conversation_id}/mes.order: (compaction | notice)? message title? (part_start delta* part_end)* context? (done | error)

/v1/chat/completions.description: Unnamed events (`data:` only), each a `chat.completion.chunk`. A failure after the headers is an error envelope on its own `data:` line, after which the stream ends; `data: [DONE]` ends a stream that finished.

message.description: One chunk, or the error envelope that ends the stream.
